targets.text: Culture Nodes runs economically and legibly: runs post live updates to Discord as devex does; model actors keep warm sessions and measurable cache economics; dispatch is budget-aware so a build never starves the operator's own Claude window; bigger work packages route to codex actors by default; a human's real-world action (merging the PR) completes their task without a second submission; failed nodes preserve their changes; and the dashboard self-refreshes with a living Node Graphs tab
the announcement holds only if every one of the seven workstreams ships with its mechanical success signal (c38) — a partial batch renders as partial delivery, never as the announced whole

Cache/usage telemetry first (#48 item 4, #47 item 2): attempts gain nullable usage_cached_input_tokens, usage_reasoning_tokens, usage_model, usage_thread_id, termination_reason via an expand-only migration on 0012's precedent; the change lands in five layers — migration, actors.Usage+ToEngine+engine.Usage (internal/actors/protocol.go:85-114), insertAttemptSQL + usage rollups + actorstats, API types + openapi.yaml Usage component, web usage domain — and the protocol's PRD-mirroring rule means §13.2 needs an ADR-style amendment (ADR-0008 precedent)
usage rows persist cached_input_tokens for codex attempts and cache_ratio is computable from stats; backends reporting no cache fields (colleague) stay NULL — never zero-filled

Session stickiness (#48 item 3, #47 item 1): continuation_ref exists only on InvocationResult (internal/actors/protocol.go:143) and completeFromResult silently drops it (internal/worker/dispatch.go:214-303) — stickiness adds it to InvocationRequest and CompletedPayload, persists it per attempt, and dispatchActor passes the prior ref for the same session key (actor+repo+workstream)
a second node turn with the same session key reaches the bridge with the prior continuation_ref populated, and a resumed session shows measurably lower uncached input than a cold one on the same task

Capacity circuit breaker (#48 item 1): a quota/session-limit class is missing from §13.5 (internal/actors/errors.go:20-47 maps provider limits to execution or auth_or_policy); Retry-After is parsed then discarded in-attempt (client.go:225); the breaker's paused-until state needs a NEW mutable table because actors rows are append-only by contract (actorstats.go:13-23), and enforcement defers work_items.available_at at the dispatch site (dispatch.go:51 area) instead of failing the attempt
a forced quota/rate/session-limit failure pauses the actor — no further dispatch reaches it until the pause expires — verified by a test observing deferred available_at, not a failed-attempt cascade

Pacing (#48 item 2) is greenfield: the worker loop is deliberately anti-pacing (a backlog drains at dispatch speed, internal/worker/worker.go:284-286) and workers scale horizontally, so a global or per-actor dispatch-rate control must be durable (DB-backed token bucket / next-dispatch-at), not an in-memory limiter
an operator-declared session rate is honored across horizontally-scaled workers (durable state, not per-process memory), and a backlog demonstrably drains no faster than the declared rate

Economic contract (#48 item 5): the only budget today is the hardcoded MaxDispatchAttempts=3 dispatch-count cap (internal/worker/worker.go:41, budget.go:65-67) — budget.max_sessions / max_uncached_input become declared workflow limits (schema + engine.Limits + run pinning) enforced at the same pre-invoke site budget.go argues for
a workflow declaring budget.max_sessions is refused at dispatch when the budget cannot fund the next session, recorded as a domain outcome — never discovered as provider exhaustion mid-wave

Discord updates ship as an out-of-process notifier daemon consuming the existing cross-run SSE feed (GET /v1alpha1/events, internal/api/events.go:183-272) and fetching human-readable detail via the read API; the control-plane process gains no Discord egress (PRD boundary rule; events carry IDs not content per internal/events/doc.go:16-25)
run-lifecycle events reach the webhook with zero Discord code or webhook URL inside the control-plane process, and a webhook outage never stalls dispatch or the SSE feed

Implement-plan mode (#45) needs an ingestion path that does not exist: internal/devague is a pure JSON-to-ledger mapper with zero production callers (no HTTP route, no CLI verb, no store) — assigning the system a plan means an import surface + durable plan/wave/task state + dashboard projection, with MapPlanWaves' wave-layering (depends_on = whole previous wave, plan.go:42-51) as the dependency shape

a devague plan can be handed to the system and appears in the dashboard with per-task status, with nothing in the ingestion path hardcoding code-repo semantics (it is instance one of the c30 generic pipeline)

Merge-as-action (#54) targets the human-inbox bridge path (Path B), not engine approval nodes: the cited live task hit_76b9a865c6132b12 is a bridge task, and the bridge already persists every non-instruction input key verbatim (extra_input, adapters/human-inbox/src/human_inbox_bridge/server.py:369) — so a declared observe: {kind: github_pr_merged, pr: N} bound into the node's input arrives and persists with zero bridge ingest changes
a human task carrying observe: github_pr_merged completes when the PR merges with no manual submit, and the ledger record names the merge commit with observed-by-tracker attribution

The merge-observer lives inside or beside the human-inbox bridge, matching spec decision c34 (the tracker that nudges is the tracker that observes): the bridge runs outside the deployment, already holds the persisted attempt-scoped HMAC callback token a days-later terminal callback needs (token TTL 15m, bridge persists it — internal/actors/token.go:35, store.py:5-12), and is stdlib-only — it would become the first bridge holding a third-party credential (GITHUB_TOKEN)
the tracker runs outside the control-plane deployment, is the only component holding the GitHub credential, and delivers the terminal callback using the bridge's persisted attempt-scoped token

The control plane never gains a GitHub credential or calls api.github.com (PRD: the control plane should not materialize provider credentials, prd-spec.md:1646; only GitHub caller today is examples/pr-upkeep/sweep.py through the runner boundary) — and #54 explicitly revises the pr-upkeep README's human-merges rule section, so that doc is edited as part of the work, never silently contradicted
grep for github credentials/api.github.com in the control-plane process stays empty after the batch, and the pr-upkeep README's human-merges section is visibly rewritten to name observed merges
Manual submit stays as the override lane (#54): tasks with no declared observable keep the inbox submit surface unchanged, covering dropped and merge-without-PR cases
a task with no declared observable behaves exactly as today, and the manual submit path still works on observed tasks (dropped / merge-without-PR cases)

Implement-plan mode (#45) reads the faithful plan view: devague plan show --json carries per-task status and real dependency edges, which nothing consumes today (MapPlanWaves deliberately reads the lossy waves view — internal/devague/plan.go:20-52); deviations already have a data model with origin user|llm and status proposed|approved (.devague/deliveries/*.json) — exactly the issue's system-knows vs user-reports split — but internal/devague has no MapDeviations and no API or web surface exposes plans
the plan view renders per-task status and real dependency edges from plan show --json (not the lossy waves view), and deviations render with origin user vs llm visibly distinguished

Discord updates port devex's proven webhook design (~120 lines) into the culture-nodes notifier: env-resolved webhook URL (never in config files — the URL embeds a token), Discord-embed payload with defensive trims, one bounded 5s POST, no retries, no redirects, strictly fail-open, outcomes journaled WITHOUT ever recording the URL or payload (devex core/webhook.py + pr/scripts/_webhook.py); devex is the only webhook POST implementation across all sibling repos and it is Python — this is a port, not an import
the notifier resolves its webhook URL from env only, posts fail-open with a bounded timeout and no retries, and journals outcomes without ever recording the URL or payload

Node Graphs tab (#56) replaces the Workflows tab (web/src/components/Header.tsx:64-66, routes/Workflows.tsx) with sub-tabs Nodes / Node Graphs / Active Graphs — the app's first sub-tab set, copying RunView's aria-pressed segmented-toggle prior art (RunView.tsx:347-367) with URL-param-driven selection for bookmarkability; the /workflows/new authoring entry point must stay reachable, and the rename touches Header.test.tsx and web/e2e/workflows.spec.ts pins
the Node Graphs tab replaces Workflows with Nodes / Node Graphs / Active Graphs sub-tabs, /workflows/new authoring stays reachable, and every existing web e2e + webglass gate stays green

New visualizations obey the culture-design contract: colors only from the pinned TERMINAL_PALETTE/TERMINAL_GROUND/NODE_KIND_PALETTE (scripts/check-culture-design.mjs pins every hex to agentculture/org sources), tokens.css stays byte-frozen, any canvas view publishes a machine-readable #agent-state mirror (webglass cannot see canvas), prefers-reduced-motion renders one static frame, and honesty condition h14 holds — everything drawn traces to a committed API row, no canned data, no decorative traffic
scripts/check-culture-design.mjs passes against the pinned org sources on the new tab, and the webglass gate (agent-state ready + zero page errors) stays green

Dashboard auto-refresh (#46): Mesh and RunView are already SSE-live; the other seven views are fetch-on-mount with zero polling and no refresh button anywhere — the fix generalizes the existing idioms (Inbox's reloadKey re-run counter, the cross-run SSE feed whose ?runs= scoping api/client.ts does not yet expose) rather than naive intervals, and must preserve the load conventions: AbortController on every fetch, agent-state 'ready' meaning initial-load-settled, stale-while-revalidate (never null a rendered list back to loading)
every dashboard view reflects new server state without a browser refresh, with stale-while-revalidate preserved — no rendered list ever nulls back to a loading state

Session resume is an all-backends change with per-backend mechanics (#47/#48): continuation_ref is hardcoded None in ALL THREE bridges (claude-code mapping.py:370, codex mapping.py:354, colleague mapping.py:340 — issue #47 understates it) and exists only on the sync 200 body while async terminal payloads omit the key entirely, yet async is the path long sessions take; claude resumes via --resume with the captured session id (already durable as claude_session_id), codex via 'codex exec resume' with the thread id (already parsed), colleague has NO resume verb in its pinned contract — an upstream colleague feature, not a bridge change; and a session_key passed via input today would be injected verbatim into the prompt's Bound-inputs block, so stickiness needs a new transport key in all three servers

claude and codex bridges resume real sessions via their native handles on both sync and async paths; colleague honestly reports no continuation (never a fabricated ref) until upstream support exists — the all-backends rule is satisfied by explicit per-backend behavior, not pretended parity

Fix fabricated codex usage on failure: codex captures usage only from turn.completed (codex_cli.py:163-166), so turn.failed and incomplete paths leave usage empty and the issue-#32 failed-attempt branch emits input_tokens:0/output_tokens:0 — fabricated zeros for sessions that burned real tokens, and failed sessions are exactly the burn #47 diagnosed; the cached_input_tokens/reasoning_output_tokens drop is pinned in the codex fixture with issue #47's exact numbers (13880/9984), while colleague's contract exposes no cache telemetry at all — its cache_ratio is honestly unmeasurable
a failed codex turn either reports its real usage or reports none (counted in attempts_not_reported) — fabricated zeros are impossible by construction and pinned by a test

Preserve-changes-on-failure (#49) lives bridge-side and needs explicit policy: workspace.py (byte-identical across the three bridges) is measurement-only — no worktree, clone, branch, commit, or stash anywhere — and bridges run in the operator's live allowlisted checkout, so preservation means committing/branching in that live tree (config knobs: commit-on-failure toggle, branch prefix, push-or-local); the post_run hook lane cannot cover it because async agent dispatch refuses post_run outright (internal/worker/hooks.go:358-383), and the all-backends asymmetry is real: colleague commits partial WIP on SIGTERM upstream, claude/codex leave uncommitted edits sitting in the tree; a dead bridge preserves nothing (in-process invocation registry)

a failed node with workspace changes leaves a commit whose message names the failure reason; when push succeeds the branch is on the remote, when push fails the local commit still exists and the run records which happened

Node granularity and actor routing (#47 item 3, the 'pass on bigger tasks / better utilize codex' ask): model nodes become work packages sized to amortize bootstrap — one persistent session with many ledgered sub-actions, not one cold session per plan task (this cycle's wave-0 tasks averaged ~25k output tokens on top of a repeated cold bootstrap) — and the split-plan lane routes big analysis/build packages to codex actors by default per the lane-cost ladder in #48's comment, keeping the operator's Claude window (one meter, many lanes: interactive session, local subagents, and claude-code bridge sessions share ONE subscription pool) for operator work; deterministic/code nodes stay microscopic

the split-plan lane declares expected model-session count per wave against the remaining window before fan-out, work packages amortize bootstrap across a shared warm session, and big analysis/build packages default to codex actors

Issue #50 is blocked upstream, not here: headspace-cli 0.11.0 supports only disabled/enabled network posture, and the runner boundary already rejects egress-allowlist honestly as rejected_input; culture-nodes' side of the fix is only to restore 'network: egress-allowlist' on the pr-upkeep sweep and pin a conformance fixture once headspace ships the allowlist — no control-plane workaround (proxy-in-process) is built in the meantime

culture-nodes ships no in-process network proxy; the sweep's declared egress-allowlist intent stays documented in the workflow comment until headspace lands it, then a conformance fixture pins the round-trip

Generic decompose pipeline (#45 reframed): the system supports splitting any source document into claims with tracked sources (the devague method productized), then splitting claims into connected decisions/actions, executing them, and verifying at the end — domain-agnostic (code, design, document writing, newsletter: scope from web -> claims -> article plan -> write -> verify); devague-plan import is one instance of this pipeline, and #45 builds on #43's split/join rather than shipping sequentially

the decompose pipeline runs end-to-end on at least one non-code domain (e.g. newsletter: web scope -> claims -> article plan -> write -> verify) with sources tracked at every step and a verification pass at the end

Node Graphs aliveness spec (#56): WebGPU is deferred by human decision, but the tab must still be stunning and feel alive on the Canvas-2D/React-Flow substrate — a faint breathing halo marks an active graph, periodic actions (heartbeat/cron checks) render visibly, all within the existing reduced-motion, agent-state-mirror, and h14 no-decorative-traffic constraints; the graph catalog derives client-side from published workflow IRs

an active graph shows a faint breathing halo and periodic actions render visibly; prefers-reduced-motion gets a static frame; the agent-state mirror stays complete; every rendered pulse traces to a committed API row (h14 — no decorative traffic)

Preserve-on-failure (#49) is commit-and-push to a recoverable branch: on node failure the bridge commits changes with the failure reason to a unique, pre-agreed branch (web-accessible on the remote), the branch name is generated by code, written to the DB, and reflected on the dashboard — recovery is possible and the operator always knows where what is; local-only commit remains the fallback when push is impossible
the preserve branch name is minted by code, stored in the DB, shown on the run detail page, and web-accessible on the remote after a successful push
Run-lifecycle Discord updates reuse DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL (the steward discord-notify channel) for now, via a CULTURE_NODES_WEBHOOK_URL-style env resolve falling back to it
updates arrive on the DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL channel and moving to a dedicated channel later is an env-only change

Observed-merge attribution (#54, decided): the tracker completes the task via the existing bridge submit path with a proposed claim carrying data.kind observed-submission and collection_method github_pr_merged plus the merge commit — honest attribution without touching the authority model or the agent-nodes-never-declare-observe compiler invariant; upgrade path recorded: graduate to runner-origin observed evidence with a RunnerManifest once manifest-bound producer registration exists

observed submissions land as proposed claims with data.kind observed-submission and collection_method github_pr_merged; no compiler or authority-model invariant changes; the runner-origin upgrade path is recorded in the exported spec

Operators of the control plane (Ori and mesh operators, now also reachable via the Discord channel), workflow authors, the actor fleet (claude-code/codex/colleague bridges on spark/thor/orin plus human actors on the inbox bridge), dashboard viewers, and the per-actor analytics consumers of #28

each named audience receives at least one shipped surface: operators get Discord updates + budget controls, authors get budget/observe contract fields, the fleet gets stickiness + honest usage, dashboard viewers get auto-refresh + Node Graphs, analytics gets cache telemetry

After shipping: every run announces its lifecycle in Discord without anyone opening the dashboard; model actors resume warm sessions and the cache economics are measurable per attempt; dispatch paces itself through the session window and trips a capacity breaker instead of cascading failed billable sessions; big work packages route to codex actors by default, preserving the operator's Claude window; a human who merges a PR is done — the system observes the merge and completes the task; a failed node leaves its changes on a pushed, DB-recorded, dashboard-visible branch; and the dashboard self-refreshes with a Node Graphs tab where active graphs visibly breathe
every after-state clause cross-maps to a confirmed requirement and a c38 signal; any orphan clause is cut or demoted at spec review

The attempts-evidence-humans-loops build proved the constraint has moved: the live fan-out exhausted the Claude 5-hour session window mid-wave (cold-session tax on ~14 bridge builds), the operator manually relayed a merge the human had already performed, and every status check required opening or refreshing the dashboard — economics and legibility, not features, now bound what the system can dogfood
the pain is cited from the recorded live build (deviation d1, issues #47/#48 diagnosis), not asserted — if the next dogfood cycle still exhausts the window mid-wave, this batch failed its own why

Mechanical, per-workstream: (1) a run completion posts to the Discord channel with no Discord code in the control plane; (2) stats expose cache_ratio and a resumed session shows measurably lower uncached input than a cold one; (3) a forced provider-limit failure pauses the actor — zero further dispatches until the pause expires — instead of a failure cascade; (4) a workflow declaring budget.max_sessions is refused at dispatch when unfundable, as a domain outcome; (5) merging a live PR completes its human task with an observed-submission claim naming the merge commit, no manual submit; (6) a failed node's changes are reachable via a branch link on the run detail page; (7) every dashboard view reflects new server state without a browser refresh; (8) the Node Graphs tab renders nodes/graphs/active-graphs derived from workflow IRs with a breathing active indicator, all web gates green
every signal is mechanically checkable (a test, a rendered element, a posted message, a ledger record) — none requires trusting an agent's completion claim

Notifier resilience: the Discord daemon keeps a durable last-event-id cursor and dedups on the outbox's stable event ids (delivery is at-least-once by design, internal/events/relay.go:58-68; the SSE surface already accepts ?from= for exactly this) — a notifier restart never silently drops or double-posts a run's lifecycle
killing and restarting the notifier mid-run produces exactly one Discord post per lifecycle event — verified by a restart test against the recorded journal

The notifier posts minimal metadata only — run id, workflow name, state, actor, and a dashboard link — never ledger records, node output, instructions, or diffs: run content is not public-by-default the way devex's PR titles are, and the events-carry-IDs-not-content rule (internal/events/doc.go:16-25) extends to what leaves for Discord
no Discord payload field is populated from ledger record data, node output, or workflow input — pinned by the payload-shaping unit tests

Preservation never disturbs the live tree: the #49 commit is built with git plumbing (write the index to a tree object, commit-tree with the failure reason, update-ref the preserve branch) so HEAD, the index, the working tree, and any concurrently-running warm session in the same checkout are untouched — bridges share the operator's live checkout (workspace.py dispatches cwd=repo), so a checkout/branch-switch approach would corrupt concurrent work
after a preserve commit, git status/HEAD/index in the operator checkout are byte-identical to the pre-preserve state, and a concurrently parked session's next turn sees no tree change it didn't make

Telemetry gates stickiness (#47's explicit ordering): before session reuse becomes default behavior, run the A/B the diagnosis prescribes — ten representative tasks through fresh sessions vs one resumed thread, comparing uncached input, cached input, session count, failures, wall time — because provider cache TTLs mean a resumed long-history session can cost MORE than a cold start; stickiness ships config-gated and flips on only with measured benefit

the A/B comparison exists as a recorded artifact before stickiness defaults on; if resumed sessions do not measurably reduce uncached input, stickiness stays opt-in and the spec's economics claims are re-examined

Pacing is reset-clock-aware (#48 comment item 5): session windows reset on a fixed clock, so the control is 'spread N sessions across the REMAINING window', not a naive fixed rate — the pacing config carries the window reset anchor and the scheduler computes remaining capacity from it
a wave started mid-window demonstrably schedules fewer sessions than the same wave started at reset, matching remaining-window arithmetic

Warm sessions serialize per session key: exactly one in-flight invocation per continuation ref — concurrent work items sharing a session_key either queue behind the active turn or deliberately fork a fresh session (recorded as such), because codex exec resume / claude --resume assume single-threaded conversations and the bridges' async runners spawn unbounded today
two simultaneous dispatches with the same session key never produce interleaved turns on one provider thread — pinned by a bridge test

Breaker and pacing decisions are observable and reversible: pausing an actor emits an engine event (visible on the dashboard and in Discord), the paused-until state renders on the actors surface, and an operator can clear a pause early via the API/CLI — budget.go's own argument (a silent skip 'stays ready forever and nothing anywhere records why') applies to the breaker exactly
a tripped breaker is diagnosable from the dashboard alone within one glance (which actor, why, until when) and clearable without touching the database

The observe declaration maps observed states to outcomes explicitly, and v1 auto-completes only the merged state (observe: {kind: github_pr_merged, pr: N} -> outcome merged): a PR closed without merging stays on the manual lane (the operator decides dropped vs retry), because #54's own override list names dropped and merge-without-PR as human-judgment cases — the tracker never guesses an outcome from an ambiguous external state
a PR closed unmerged does NOT auto-complete its task; only the merged state produces an automatic submission — pinned by a tracker test

Auto-refresh shares one event stream: the app opens a single app-wide EventSource (a shared provider/context over the cross-run feed) that views subscribe to, instead of each view opening its own — browsers cap concurrent connections per origin (6 on HTTP/1.1), and Mesh + RunView already hold two; per-view EventSources across seven more views would starve the cap in multi-tab use
opening every dashboard view across two tabs holds at most one SSE connection per tab, and view-level subscriptions attach/detach without reconnecting the stream

Parallel tokens ship in full (#43, per q8): the engine honors limits.maxParallelTokens, transition plans grow multi-edge splits and join barriers with per-token bounds, and event-driven continuation lands whole — a node emits events non-blocking mid-execution and any subscribed node picks them up, including as splits; the c9 groundwork (token parent links, multi-waiter signal_subscriptions) is the substrate, and event-then-subscription replay (the 0016 documented gap) is closed as part of this

a workflow declaring maxParallelTokens > 1 demonstrably runs concurrent tokens through a split and reconverges at a join with bounds enforced, and an event emitted mid-execution resumes a waiter that subscribed AFTER emission (replay closed) — both pinned by engine tests

tasks.summary: Extend attempt usage: expand-only migration adding usage_cached_input_tokens, usage_reasoning_tokens, usage_model, usage_thread_id, termination_reason; actors.Usage + ToEngine + engine.Usage; insertAttemptSQL params; ADR amending PRD section 13.2
acceptance_criteria: migration applies over N-1 rows with no backfill and a round-trip test persists and reads all five new fields as nullable
ADR committed citing the ADR-0008 precedent for protocol-field additions

tasks.summary: Expose extended usage: usage rollups, NodeRunUsages, and actor stats aggregate the new fields; openapi Usage component + API types; web usage domain computes and renders cache_ratio in Statistics
acceptance_criteria: run detail and actor stats responses include cached_input_tokens and a computable cache_ratio, rendered in the web Statistics view
web mergeUsage mirrors the server aggregation rules for the new fields (unit test)

tasks.summary: Bridge usage honesty (all three backends): emit cached_input, reasoning, model, thread or session id, and termination reason where the backend reports them; codex captures usage from failed and incomplete turns; truly absent usage emits NO block, never zeros; colleague cache fields stay null
acceptance_criteria: codex fixture round-trips cached_input_tokens 9984 of 13880 into the completed payload
a codex turn.failed test shows either real usage or an absent block counted as attempts_not_reported — zero-filled usage is unrepresentable
colleague mapping test pins cache fields as null, not zero

tasks.summary: Engine continuation carriage: continuation_ref lands on InvocationRequest and CompletedPayload, persists per attempt, and dispatchActor populates the prior ref for the same session key
acceptance_criteria: engine test: the next attempt's request carries the ref the prior completion returned; absent refs dispatch clean
async completion persists the ref on the attempt row

tasks.summary: Bridge session resume (all three backends): claude resumes with its captured session id, codex with its exec resume verb; the ref returns on sync AND async terminal payloads; session_key becomes a transport key excluded from Bound-inputs injection in all three servers; colleague honestly returns a null ref and an upstream feature request is filed
acceptance_criteria: per-bridge test pins the resume argv given a prior ref, and the async terminal payload carries continuation_ref
transport-key test proves session_key never appears in the prompt text
colleague bridge returns ref null and the upstream issue link is recorded

tasks.summary: Session-key serialization and bridge concurrency config: exactly one in-flight invocation per session key (concurrent same-key work queues or deliberately forks, recorded as such); in-flight caps join the shared bridge config surface
acceptance_criteria: two simultaneous same-key dispatches never interleave turns on one provider thread (bridge test)
concurrency config keys parse with sane defaults in all three bridges

tasks.summary: Stickiness A/B gate: ten representative tasks through fresh sessions vs one resumed thread; comparison artifact (uncached input, cached input, sessions, failures, wall time) recorded; stickiness stays opt-in until the artifact shows uncached-input reduction
acceptance_criteria: comparison artifact committed with the five measured columns and a verdict
default-on is config-gated on the artifact's verdict

tasks.summary: Capacity error class: section 13.5 gains capacity_exhausted; provider quota, rate, and session-limit failures classify to it; the class and Retry-After persist on the attempt instead of being discarded in-attempt
acceptance_criteria: classification tests map provider-limit response shapes to capacity_exhausted
the attempt row carries the error class and any Retry-After value

tasks.summary: Circuit breaker: new mutable actor_availability table (actors stays append-only); dispatch-site check defers work_items.available_at instead of failing the attempt; pause emits an engine event; paused state renders on the actors API; manual clear via API and CLI
acceptance_criteria: a forced provider-limit failure pauses the actor and zero further dispatches reach it until expiry (worker + store test)
the pause is visible on the actors surface with reason and until-when, and clearable without touching the database

tasks.summary: Pacing: durable dispatch-rate state (per actor and global) consulted at the dispatch site, honored identically across horizontally-scaled workers; reset-clock arithmetic spreads sessions across the remaining window
acceptance_criteria: two worker processes sharing one database jointly honor a declared rate (integration test)
a wave started mid-window schedules per remaining-window arithmetic (unit test)

tasks.summary: Budget contract: budget.max_sessions and max_uncached_input as declared workflow limits (schema, engine.Limits, run pinning); pre-invoke enforcement refuses unfundable dispatch as a routable domain outcome; counting charges cold session starts, not resumed warm turns
acceptance_criteria: a workflow declaring an unfundable wave is refused at dispatch as a domain outcome that routes an edge (worker test)
a warm workstream of N node turns consumes 1 from max_sessions, not N (engine test)

tasks.summary: Routing and granularity guidance: the split-plan lane and nodes-operator skill document work-package node sizing, a per-wave model-session-count declaration against the remaining window, and the codex-first default for big analysis and build packages
acceptance_criteria: assign-to-workforce and nodes-operator guidance updated; the split-plan template carries a session-count-per-wave declaration

tasks.summary: Webhook layer (Go port of devex's design): env resolve CULTURE_NODES_WEBHOOK_URL falling back to DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL; minimal-metadata Discord embed (run id, workflow, state, actor, dashboard link only); one bounded 5s fail-open POST, no retries, no redirects; outcomes journaled without URL or payload; hermetic test pattern with a separate TEST env var
acceptance_criteria: payload-shaping tests prove no embed field derives from ledger records, node output, or workflow input
the live-network test gates on a separate TEST url env var and an autouse fixture unsets production vars for the whole suite

tasks.summary: Discord notifier daemon: out-of-process SSE consumer over the cross-run events feed with a durable last-event-id cursor and stable-id dedup; human-readable detail fetched via the read API; zero control-plane changes
acceptance_criteria: kill-and-restart mid-run posts exactly one Discord message per lifecycle event (restart test over the journal)
the daemon builds and runs without any control-plane code change

tasks.summary: Observable declaration: authoring convention binds an observe block (kind github_pr_merged, pr number) into the human-task node's input; example workflow updated; the tracker contract documented
acceptance_criteria: a declared observable round-trips into the bridge's stored extra_input untouched (bridge test)
the example workflow carries the declaration bound from a prior node's output

tasks.summary: Merge tracker beside the human-inbox bridge: stdlib-only poller holding GITHUB_TOKEN, watches declared observables, auto-submits ONLY the merged state through the existing submit surface as an observed-submission claim (collection_method github_pr_merged, merge commit named); closed-unmerged and undeclared tasks stay manual; manual submit still works on observed tasks
acceptance_criteria: a merged PR completes its task with the observed-submission claim naming the merge commit (tracker test on recorded fixtures)
a PR closed without merging does not auto-complete
manual submission on an observed task succeeds unchanged

tasks.summary: Human-merges doc revision and credential gate: rewrite the pr-upkeep README's human-merges section to define approved as the observed merge; add a gate proving the control-plane process holds no GitHub credential and never calls the GitHub API
acceptance_criteria: the README section is rewritten to name observed merges
a grep gate over control-plane sources finds no GitHub credential or api.github.com caller

tasks.summary: Nudge transport: one discord-bot-cli thread per parked human attempt (create + mention), tracker-owned cadence with its own throttle, reply relay via channel-messages polling; severity color, username, and timestamp embed vocabulary lifted from steward's discord-notify
acceptance_criteria: a parked human attempt produces one thread and one nudge post (fixture test)
a reply posted in-thread is relayed to the run as a progress update

risks.text: Bridge-host push credentials unverified: the preserve push leg assumes thor and orin service environments hold a writable git credential — never checked; local-commit fallback carries until ops confirms
Daemon placement and secret custody: where the notifier and merge tracker run (thor beside the API vs spark) is undecided; webhook URL and bot token live in an interactive shell today
Full split/join is the largest engine change since phase 0; the design pass may surface schema or state-model needs beyond the current groundwork
Colleague upstream resume support has no committed timeline; stickiness ships two-backends-real, one-backend-honest until it lands
GitHub API rate limits bound the merge tracker's polling cadence across many parked tasks; cadence needs a budget before the tracker scales
